newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-WMC says economies weigh on metals.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-WMC says economies weigh on metals.

text.p: Diminished growth prospects in the main industrialised countries led to weaker prices for most nonferrous metals and gold in the December quarter, diversified Australian resources company WMC Ltd said on Tuesday.

WMC also said the prices it received for most of the commodities it produces were substantially lower in the half-year ended December 31 compared with the corresponding period a year earlier. "Furthermore, Australian-dollar revenues were reduced by a much stronger Australian dollar when compared to the first six months of 1995-96," WMC said.
Nickel demand from the stainless steel industry was steady in the December quarter, WMC said.

However, market sentiment for the metal was affected negatively by rising inventories at the London Metal Exchange, the company said in a statement accompanying its latest quarterly commodities production report.

"The market for smelter-grade alumina improved marginally on the basis of better metals prices," WMC said. "After very thin spot trades at around US$148 a tonne for most of the quarter, spot prices have subsequently improved to US$175 a tonne."
In gold, WMC linked forward selling by miners and selling by central banks and fund manager to a fall in the international gold price to US$369.00 an ounce from US$380.00 during the quarter.
Recent volatility in copper prices stemmed from strong demand for immediate delivery of metal and considerably reduced LME inventories, WMC said.
Steady declines in LME copper inventories had left the market with a stocks-to-consumption ratio of about four days, WMC said.

In uranium, spot market prices continued a weakening trend through the close of calendar 1996 as the key buyers of the metal, utility companies, deferred spot purchases in the expectation of securing more favourable terms for 1997, WMC said.
Uranium fetched only US$14.70 a pound on average in December versus US$15.40 in October, it said.
At 0430 GMT (3.30 p.m.), WMC shares were trading five cents lower at A$8.26
